Single EM step: E-step responsibilities + M-step update of A, mu, and all non-parametric background/triggering components

Source: R/em_step.R
em_step.Rd

Single EM step: E-step responsibilities + M-step update of A, mu, and all non-parametric background/triggering components

Usage

em_step(
  events,
  background,
  trend,
  weekly,
  monthly,
  temporal_trigger,
  spatial_trigger,
  mu,
  A,
  pairs,
  cache_dir,
  cell_size,
  nprocs = 1,
  exclude_self = TRUE,
  bgint = NULL,
  trig = NULL,
  marks = NULL
)

Arguments

events

A semihawkes_events object (from prepare_events(), already passed through add_adaptive_bandwidth() / add_bg_integral()).

background

A semihawkes_spatial_base object from the previous iteration's background_spatial() call (only its grid/marks are reused as the spatial domain; a fresh weighted surface is computed inside this step).

trend, weekly, monthly

The previous iteration's semihawkes_temporal_base objects (weekly/monthly/trend).

temporal_trigger, spatial_trigger

The previous iteration's triggering-kernel objects.

mu, A

The previous iteration's scalar parameter estimates.

pairs

A trigger_pairs() index (built once, reused every iteration – it does not depend on the current parameter estimates).

cache_dir

Directory populated by trigger_spatial_marks() (built once, reused every iteration – depends only on spatial_trigger's grid, which is fixed across iterations).

cell_size

Passed to background_spatial().

nprocs

Passed to trigger_evaluate(): a whole number of parallel workers (1, the default, runs serially), "auto", or a cluster from parallel::makeCluster(). A number or "auto" starts new workers at every call; to reuse them across steps, pass a cluster, as fit_semihawkes() does.

exclude_self

Passed to trigger_evaluate(); default TRUE.

bgint, trig

Optional. The results of background_intensity() and trigger_evaluate() for exactly the background, trend, weekly, monthly and triggering kernels passed in, as returned in $bgint and $trig by the previous call to em_step(). Supplying them saves evaluating the same quantities again at the start of this step; the result is the same. NULL (the default) evaluates them here. Values computed for any other inputs give wrong results.

marks

Optional: the spatial marks in cache_dir, already read into a list with one logical matrix per event, as fit_semihawkes() does once per fit. Passed to trigger_edge_correction(); NULL (the default) reads them from cache_dir at this step.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_em_step" with the updated mu, A, llik, lambda_at_all, lambda_at_events, bgprobs, the refreshed background, trend, weekly, monthly, temporal_trigger, spatial_trigger objects, and bgint and trig, the background intensity and triggering contributions evaluated with those refreshed components – everything needed to feed straight into the next call to em_step().

Examples

# \donttest{
# A quick fit to one year of the bundled simulated data: a coarse grid, a
# coarse triggering-kernel grid and two EM iterations keep it to a few
# seconds. Real analyses need finer settings and more iterations.
cache_dir <- tempfile("spHawkes_marks_")
fit <- fit_semihawkes(
  sim_events, sim_region,
  date_col  = "date",
  end_date  = "2022-01-01",
  cell_size = 1000,
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  trigger_spatial_args = list(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250),
  trigger_window_dist  = 2000,
  n_iter  = 2,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed    = 1
)
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
# One more EM step from where the fit stopped
pairs <- trigger_pairs(fit$events, window_days = 90, window_dist = 2000)
step <- em_step(fit$events, fit$background, fit$trend, fit$weekly,
                fit$monthly, fit$temporal_trigger, fit$spatial_trigger,
                mu = fit$mu, A = fit$A, pairs = pairs,
                cache_dir = cache_dir, cell_size = 1000)
step
#> <semihawkes_em_step>
#>   mu = 2.55376e-09, A = 0.559732, llik = -1873.06, lambda_at_all = 98
# }
